predecessors.name: Sunda Kingdom
predecessors.text: the coast 'between Brebes and Indramayu', a principality within Sunda from 1445-1447 that Sunda 'has lost control of' by 1513

successors.name: Kasepuhan Sultanate
successors.text: the Kasepuhan line of Muhammad Samsudin (1677-1703)

successors.name: Kanoman Sultanate
successors.text: the Kanoman line of Muhammad Badruddin (1677-1723)

rulers.name: Sunan Gunungjati (Sharif Hidayatullah, Sultan Cirebon I)
Panembahan Ratu II / Girilaya (Sultan Cirebon III)

ledger.x: 2 April 1482: Sunan Gunungjati stops Cirebon's tribute to Pajajaran.

1526: Banten conquered; its king Hasanuddin is Cirebon's vassal under Demak's auspices (infobox 'Syarif Hidayatullah conquered Banten: 1526'; the Sunda Kingdom page: 'Sunan Gunungjati of Cirebon later crowned his son, Hasanuddin, as the king of Banten').
1552: Banten becomes independent of Cirebon (infobox 'Independence from Cirebon Sultanate: 1552').
1677: the Kanoman share goes to Muhammad Badruddin.
1677: the Keprabonan share goes to Nasruddin.
1677: the sultanate of Cirebon ends in the three-way partition.

wars.name: Cirebon-Demak war on Sunda
wars.outcome: Banten (1526) and Sunda Kalapa (1527, renamed Jayakarta) taken by Cirebon-Demak forces; King Surawisesa of Sunda made peace with Cirebon in 1531.

wars.name: Cirebon's suppression of the Sumedang and Ciamis rebellions
wars.outcome: Cirebon, asked by Sultan Agung to help against Batavia, defeated the Sumedang and Ciamis rebellions in 1618 and 1619; no land passed to Cirebon.

wars.name: Pagarage (Pacirebonan) war
wars.outcome: Banten's navy beat Mataram's about sixty ships with Cirebonese troops off Tanara; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Banten's hold on Cirebon and its loss
wars.outcome: Tirtayasa installed the Cirebon princes at Banten in 1677; the Dutch allied with Mataram and fought Banten 'for two years', forcing it to give up control of Cirebon; Cirebon then passed from Mataram to the Dutch as a protectorate.

certainty.note: A coastal principality whose reach is a stretch of coast and a handful of vassal claims; no treaty line is dated by the pages opened.
